sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Oak Park, Michigan?
sections.html:
You list it, sell it yourself, or take an offer from a buyer who purchases houses directly. In Oak Park the paperwork after any of these runs through three offices: the city assessor, the city's Municipal Services Department, and the Oakland County Register of Deeds.

Much of Oak Park was built in the postwar boom described below, so a seller often has a house with decades of updates, some of them done with permits and some not. That history affects which route fits. A buyer using a mortgage will order an inspection and an appraisal, while a direct buyer prices the repairs into the offer. Ask each buyer to put the closing date, repair terms and your net amount in writing, and compare offers on what reaches you after closing.

Start with the paperwork you can control: pull your last deed, find permit records for the roof, furnace and electrical work, and gather the water and utility account details. Each of those items shows up at a different point in the sale.

sections.h2: What is Oak Park like as a place to own a house?
sections.html:
Oak Park is an inner-ring suburb that borders Detroit on its south edge, about 14 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. It covers 5.16 square miles, all land. Eight Mile Road (M-102) is the southern boundary and the Oakland and Wayne county line, Eleven Mile Road marks the north, and Greenfield Road runs along the west. I-696 crosses the northern edge and the Lodge Freeway (M-10) is close by (Wikipedia, Oak Park).

The first big subdivision went in during 1914, the area became a village in 1927 and a city on October 29, 1945. Between 1950 and 1960 the population rose from about 5,000 to more than 36,000, and the city carried the label of fastest growing in America. The city annexed parts of Royal Oak Township in 2002 and 2004, and a FedEx distribution center on a 60-acre former armory site opened on March 31, 2017.

The Census Bureau puts Oak Park at 29,072 residents as of July 1, 2025, down 1.7% from the 2020 base. Population density was 5,743.2 people per square mile in 2020, the densest of the four cities in this set, so houses sit close together and street-by-street comparisons matter.

sections.h2: What do the housing numbers say about Oak Park?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median value of an owner-occupied Oak Park home at $212,300 and median gross rent at $1,396. Owners occupy 63.3% of homes, and the city has 12,452 households with a median income of $71,510.

  • Persons per household: 2.35.
  • Share of residents aged 65 or older: 17.4%.
  • Persons in poverty: 12.0%.
  • Mean travel time to work: 23.3 minutes.

Each year the city assessor posts a sales study. The 2026 assessment year study covers sales from April 1, 2023 through March 31, 2025, and the city publishes an economic condition factor report that residents can look up by parcel on BSAonline.com. Those two documents show how the assessor values houses like yours, which is useful context before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Which Oak Park school district is a house in?
sections.html:
Most of the city belongs to Oak Park Schools. Students living between 10 Mile and 11 Mile Roads are in the Berkley School District, and about a square mile on the east end is in Ferndale Public Schools.

Because a boundary can run along a street, a buyer asking about schools needs the exact address checked. That matters most for homes on the north strip near I-696, where Berkley applies.

sections.h2: What city fees and inspections affect an Oak Park sale?
sections.html:
Oak Park charges set fees for occupancy, rental registration and alarm permits, and a few of them come up when a house changes hands. The table lists the ones printed on the city's pages.

Oak Park city charges that can come up in a sale
ItemWhat the city page says
Certificate of occupancy$50 for occupancy only or reissuance
Rental registration$80 for two years
Rental inspection$150, due every two years or after a change in tenancy
Emergency alarm permit$20 one time; each change in ownership of an operable alarm needs a new permit
Garage sale permit$10, required for any residential garage sale

The certificate of occupancy is required before a new or altered building is used or occupied, and applications go to the Municipal Services Department at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard. Landlords who sell a tenant-occupied house should know the city expects rentals to pass inspection before occupancy, so a house that was vacant between tenants may need that inspection before it can be occupied again.

sections.h2: Which permits should an Oak Park seller have on file?
sections.html:
Oak Park lists separate permits for building, electrical and demolition work, and the Building Division at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard takes the building permit application. The city also publishes Roofing Guidelines for Residential Properties, which explain the roofing-permit process and the inspections a roofing project requires.

If your roof, wiring or an addition was done by a previous owner, ask the Municipal Services Department what is on record for the address. A missing final inspection is easier to fix before you list than after a buyer's inspector finds it. The city code also requires owners, occupants and tenants to maintain the property around their buildings, so clear overgrowth, debris and broken fencing before showings.

Clearing out a house is part of many sales. A residential garage sale needs a $10 permit from the City Clerk's Office, and the clerk's page asks for a state ID or driver's license showing the sale address.

sections.h2: What must a seller file with the Oak Park assessor?
sections.html:
The assessor's office is at 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. Two forms matter after a sale.

  • Property Transfer Affidavit: required whenever ownership of real property changes, including title, beneficial use or ownership interest, and due within 45 days of the transfer.
  • Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption: homeowners who sell or convert their principal residence file it to remove the exemption.

Buyers file their own exemption form after closing. Ask the title company which of these it submits on your behalf so nothing is filed twice or missed.

sections.h2: How does the Oakland County deed record work for an Oak Park house?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds, which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Its fee page states that county transfer tax is $.55 per $500.00 and state transfer tax is $3.75 per $500.00 of consideration, and that a deed with consideration under $100.00 is exempt. The reason for any exemption must appear on the face of the document.

The office's questions page lists a few other requirements a seller can check in advance: a 2-1/2 inch top margin, notarized signatures, and an embossed seal on any death certificate that is submitted. Its public index can find recorded documents back to January 1, 1964, so you can pull your own prior deed to confirm the legal description before you sign.

faqs.q: Does Oak Park require an inspection before I can sell my house?
faqs.a: The city pages list a certificate of occupancy for new or altered buildings and a rental inspection every two years or after a change in tenancy. Ask the Municipal Services Department whether your house, especially if it has been rented, needs either before the buyer moves in.

faqs.q: What does a certificate of occupancy cost in Oak Park?
faqs.a: The city's fee schedule prints $50 for a certificate of occupancy covering occupancy only and $50 for reissuance. Commercial and renovation certificates have different amounts on the same schedule.

faqs.q: Do I need to cancel my alarm permit when I sell in Oak Park?
faqs.a: The city's alarm permit page says there is a one-time $20 fee and that each change in ownership of an operable alarm system requires a new permit. Tell the buyer so they register the system under their name.

faqs.q: How soon must the Property Transfer Affidavit be filed in Oak Park?
faqs.a: It is due within 45 days of the transfer, filed with the Assessor's Office at 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. The form applies to any change in title, beneficial use or ownership interest.

faqs.q: Which county office records the deed for an Oak Park house?
faqs.a: The Oakland County Register of Deeds records it. Warranty deeds are tax certified at the county treasurer's office first, for a $5.00 fee, and the recording fee is $30.00.
